newsitem.title: USA: Muni yield curve steepens over past week - Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni yield curve steepens over past week - Delphis.

text.p: The municipal yield curve steepened about five basis points in the week ended Wednesday, as yield increases in long-term securities outpaced the short-end.
The Baa yield curve between one-year and thirty-year bonds steepened five basis points to 200 basis points. The triple-A yield curve, however, was unchanged at 200 basis points.

Muni yields have been on a steady upward course for several weeks, following the Treasury market higher. But long-term municipals again underperformed the government market, as the yield on the Treasury's 30-year bond dropped one basis point on the week, moving to 6.98 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated municipal yields, in contrast, rose five basis points to 5.75 percent. Thirty-year Baa yields rose 10 basis points to 6.60 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis were yielding 82.4 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Wednesday.
Average yields on one-year municipal bonds rose five basis points across the credit spectrum, rising to 3.75 percent in the Aaa category and to 4.60 percent for Baa's.
Yields rose 10 basis points in the intermediate sector, moving ten-year Aaa-rated bonds to 5.05 percent and Baa-rated ten-years to 5.90 percent.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged at 85 basis points, and the 30-year spread widened five to 85 basis points.
